blocks.text: Why adjusters choose Chrome on Mac

Many claims systems are built for the web. Chrome provides a stable environment for these platforms. Mac users often prefer Chrome because it handles multiple tabs well. You can keep your email, your claims portal, and your photo storage open at the same time. This reduces the need to switch between apps constantly.
Essential Chrome shortcuts for claims work

Speed matters when you have a long list of claims to process. Memorizing a few shortcuts will save you minutes every hour. Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab for a quick search. Use ⌘ + L to jump immediately to the address bar. If you need to find a specific claim number on a long page, press ⌘ + F to open the search bar. Type your claim number, and Chrome will highlight every instance on the screen.

items: ⌘ + L: Jump to the address bar
⌘ + F: Find text on the page
Control + Tab: Switch to the next tab

blocks.text: You likely work with several insurance carriers. Each one might require a different login. Mixing your cookies and saved passwords can lead to errors. The best way to manage this is to create a unique Chrome profile for each carrier. Go to your profile icon in the top right corner. Select Add to create a new profile. You can name it after the carrier. Now your bookmarks and passwords for that specific system stay separate from your other work.

Writing reports takes up to 4 hours a day for many adjusters. Lazur helps you get through this faster by letting you speak your notes. Hold the fn key and start talking. Lazur will type your observations into the text box in your browser. You can dictate your field notes while looking at your photos. This keeps your hands free and your focus on the evidence.

Sometimes a claims portal will stop loading correctly. This is often due to corrupted site data. You do not need to clear your entire history. You can clear data for just one site. Click the settings icon or the lock icon in the address bar. Select Site settings. From there, you can clear data for that specific domain. This often fixes the Aw, Snap error without losing your other saved logins.

A cluttered screen slows you down. Use the Mac Mission Control feature to keep your claims work in one space. Swipe up with three fingers on your trackpad to see all your open windows. You can drag your Chrome window to a separate desktop space. This keeps your email and your claims system from overlapping. You can swipe left or right to move between them.
Using Lazur to find buttons in complex portals

Some insurance portals have cluttered interfaces. You might spend time looking for the Save or Submit button. Instead of scanning the page, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the button is. Lazur will look at your screen and draw a circle around the button for you. This is a quick way to find what you need without hunting through menus.

Extensions can help you manage your time. However, too many extensions can make Chrome slow. Review your extensions regularly. Click the puzzle piece icon in the toolbar to manage them. Disable any that you do not use daily. If you use a specific tool for photo management, keep only that one active. This keeps your browser fast for heavy tasks like uploading large claim files.

If you are an independent adjuster, you are often working from your car or a hotel. Use the Chrome Reading List to save articles or policy documents for later. Click the bookmark icon and select Add to Reading List. You can access these offline if you sync your tabs beforehand. This ensures you have the information you need even when your connection is weak.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in my claims software?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or interact with the software for you. It can point to buttons by drawing a circle on your screen or guide you through a process one step at a time.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my claim data?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut key. The screenshot and audio are sent to AI providers to answer your request and are never stored or used to train models.

faq.question: How do I speed up Chrome on my Mac?
faq.answer: You can speed up Chrome by clearing site data for specific websites, disabling unused extensions, and keeping your browser updated to the latest version.

faq.question: Is Chrome better than Safari for insurance portals?
faq.answer: Many insurance portals are optimized for Chrome. If a site is not working in Safari, Chrome is often the recommended alternative by IT departments.
